review_notes: Read the whole target file and the definitions of HahnSeries.filter, coeff_filter, support_filter and support_filter_subset in Truncation.lean. Checked Mathlib's support_one (it is simp) and the uses of restrictToAddSubgroup/coe_restrictToAddSubgroup elsewhere. The only simp attribute in the file, coe_restrictToAddSubgroup, is a reasonable rfl lemma, and I found no loop or competing rule. The finding is a missing membership-level simp lemma upstream of the file. It is modest and I did not run Lean. I did not check every other file that uses support_filter to count the call sites precisely.

findings.problem: The simp interface for `HahnSeries.filter` has `coeff_filter` as @[simp], but its support lemma `support_filter` is not simp. It is stated only as a set equality `{i ∈ x.support | p i}`. There is also no pointwise membership lemma `g ∈ (filter p x).support ↔ g ∈ x.support ∧ p g`. The file therefore unfolds `set` abbreviations by hand and rewrites with `support_filter` at the same pattern four times (lines 79, 130, 134, 175). Each time it then projects with `hg.1` and `hg.2`, and it needs `rw [hr/hq_def, …] at …` because `simp` has no rule to use. This is a canonical-form gap: the natural normal form for membership in a restricted support is a conjunction, and no rule produces it.
findings.proposed_change: In Truncation.lean, next to `support_filter`, add a lemma of the form `@[simp] theorem mem_support_filter (p : G → Prop) [DecidablePred p] (x : R⟦G⟧) (i : G) : i ∈ (filter p x).support ↔ i ∈ x.support ∧ p i`. Prove it from `coeff_filter`/`mem_support`, or from `support_filter` with `Set.mem_sep_iff`. Then the four call sites become `simpa [hr] using hg`, or `(by simpa [hr_def] using hg : _ ∧ _)`. It is better to add the iff lemma rather than make the set-builder `support_filter` itself simp, because the iff gives a stable conjunction normal form and avoids leaving `{i ∈ _ | _}` terms around.
findings.benefit: Membership in the support of a restricted series would normalize to `g ∈ x.support ∧ p g` under `simp`. Support-chasing steps like the ones in these factorization proofs would not need manual `rw` with `set` variables and `.1`/`.2` projections, and other files that rewrite with `support_filter` (e.g. ClosedClassRefinementTransport.lean line 183) could use the same lemma.

evidence.excerpt:
theorem support_filter (p : G → Prop) [DecidablePred p] (x : R⟦G⟧) :
    (filter p x).support = {i ∈ x.support | p i}

@[simp]
protected theorem coeff_filter (p : G → Prop) [DecidablePred p] (x : R⟦G⟧) (i : G) :

rw [hq_def, HahnSeries.support_filter] at hg
    exact hg.2
